semantics.note: The normalization preserves the assessment of recurring failures across the cited domains, without claiming that models never reason or cannot improve.

contract.note: Repeated failures across controlled variations and multiple domains are a fair plain reading. The contract appropriately treats chess as anecdotal and separates behavioral robustness from internal causes.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous study documents repeated mathematical failures across models and controlled variations. Its behavioral results support the claim without establishing its proposed internal explanation.
Systematic degradation on larger and obfuscated planning problems supports recurring weaknesses. Strong simpler-task performance and substantial improvement qualify their scope without refuting them.
Testing 25 models on 10,552 variations independently corroborates recurring mathematical robustness failures, while also documenting resilient categories and useful prompting improvements.
Author-reported success with specialized chess fine-tuning qualifies generalizations from anecdotes. The different models and single-move task do not overturn the combined math and planning pattern.
Available before the cutoff, this later experiment raises a relevant ambiguity concern. Its new distractors and later testing period prevent it from directly overturning the historical findings.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous math and planning studies document repeated failures across substantial test sets and controlled variations, satisfying the fair plain-reading contract. Easier-task successes, specialized chess results and the later distractor audit limit broader conclusions but do not erase this pattern. The evidence does not establish a shared internal cause or universal inability to reason.
